issues.title: Campaign-wide counter ownership is not pinned
issues.details: SPEC.md requires five total attempts across a doctor probe, text extraction, separate text labeling, image extraction, and optional image labeling, while graphify/llm.py currently contains recursive adaptive extraction and label retries. The artifact says a validation counter aborts before request six and that an unexpected failure stops the campaign, but it does not explicitly state that one counter persists across the separate CLI processes or how an unexpected result prevents Graphify-level retry entry points from issuing another request before control returns. A process-local counter could reset between commands, and a post-hoc tally cannot fail closed before request six. This is a planning-handoff ambiguity, not a blocker at the inspected pre-implementation-planning phase.
issues.suggested_fix: The implementation plan should assign one campaign-scope counter owner shared across every canary command and define pre-dispatch counting/denial plus fail-fast treatment of Graphify adaptive and label retries. Process-local and manual/post-hoc accounting should be explicitly rejected.

verification_gaps: No Pi implementation, implementation plan, new provenance tests, campaign counter, or live canary evidence exists in the inspected phase.
The named Luna evaluation document was not inspected because model-quality and transport evidence were outside this three-issue recheck.
Fresh graphify-out artifacts were not used because canonical source and test files directly established the relevant current behavior.
recommended_fixes: Carry the single campaign-wide counter owner and Graphify-retry fail-fast rule into planning; no further artifact-review round is necessary for this WARN.
review.core_challenge: Ensure the new safety contracts match existing cache, labeling, and retry boundaries without demanding implementation detail beyond the current specification-to-planning phase.
assumptions_to_verify: Image provenance will be stamped from trusted attachment state rather than model-produced output and preserved through incremental cache merges.
The validation counter will be shared across all separate canary commands and incremented before dispatching each attempted Pi request.
An unexpected canary failure will prevent Graphify adaptive splitting or label retry from silently consuming another attempt.
technical_reality: Current semantic cache entries contain nodes, edges, hyperedges, and optional partial state but no image-delivery provenance; historical raster entries therefore cannot prove pixel delivery.
Current image routing can strip pixels for a non-vision backend and retain only a reference, establishing the need for pixel-derived versus reference-only provenance.
Current cluster-only behavior computes deterministic hub labels, overlays only non-placeholder generated labels, and avoids persisting intentionally placeholder-only output.
Current extraction and label owners can recursively split and retry up to configured depth, so a live-call budget must govern those internal requests as well as top-level commands.
The inspected lifecycle source places this work before implementation planning; SPEC.md likewise describes its commands as contracts for later planning and validation.
spec_gaps: The live-validation counter is not explicitly defined as one cross-process campaign resource, and the interaction between fail-fast campaign behavior and existing Graphify retry recursion is not pinned.
downstream_risks: A process-local or post-hoc counter could let the complete canary campaign exceed five Pi requests despite each individual command appearing compliant.
